subject.title: Bug: preflight (budget-triggered) compaction hard-capped at ~60s, ignores compaction.timeoutSeconds

question: Should OpenClaw make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95590 the canonical fix for this issue's preflight compaction cancellation contract, while leaving a preflight disable config gate as separate work?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the remaining choice is maintainer-owned behavior: which reply abort reasons should cancel required preflight compaction, and whether to add another config surface.

options.title: Use the linked cancellation fix
options.body: Accept the filtered-signal contract so lifecycle TimeoutError no longer caps required preflight compaction while explicit user/restart cancellation still propagates.

options.title: Require exact slow-backend proof first
options.body: Keep the issue and PR open until a maintainer or reporter supplies redacted proof from the same class of slow local backend described in the issue.

options.title: Prioritize a config gate instead
options.body: Defer the cancellation fix and sponsor a separate `compaction.preflight.enabled` config decision, accepting that the existing timeout bug remains until that direction lands.

recommendation.title: Use the linked cancellation fix
recommendation.body: Accept the filtered-signal contract so lifecycle TimeoutError no longer caps required preflight compaction while explicit user/restart cancellation still propagates.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the affected preflight compaction path is the merged transcript-estimate preflight work in `agent-runner-memory.ts`.
